newsitem.title: ROMANIA: White House optimistic on tax cut legislation.
newsitem.headline: White House optimistic on tax cut legislation.

text.p: President Bill Clinton believes it is "quite likely" a bipartisan compromise will emerge from Congressional negotiations on a balanced budget, White House spokesman Mike McCurry said on Friday.

"I think the President's view is that the spirit of bipartisanship is holding on the Hill (Congress) and that the likelihood of tax cut legislation and spending legislation that reflects the bipartisan balanced budget agreement is still quite likely," McCurry told reporters in Romania, where Clinton was visiting after the NATO summit.
He said Clinton will meet with Republican and Democratic Congressional leaders on Capitol Hill on Tuesday next week to discuss the status of the tax- and spending-cut legislation.
McCurry said Clinton also would use his weekly radio address Saturday to express his strong support for tax cuts and repeat his tax cut priorities in the negotiations with Congress.
Senate and House negotiators are trying to reconcile the differences between their competing tax cut bills and Clinton has expressed strong reservations about some of the Republican proposals.
